heroHeadline: Pakistan Summons Afghan Envoy Over Bannu Attack on Day 75; COAS Vows Fight Against TTP Facilitators Until 'Logical Conclusion'
heroSubtitle: On May 11, 2026 (Day 75 of Operation Ghazab lil-Haq), Pakistan summoned the Afghan Chargé d'Affaires in Islamabad and issued a strong demarche over the May 10 Bannu suicide car bomb and drone attack that killed at least 15 Khyber Pakhtunkhwa police officers. Pakistan conveyed that technical intelligence confirmed the attack was 'masterminded by terrorists residing in Afghanistan' — directly implicating the Afghan Taliban government for providing sanctuary to the Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan alliance and Hafiz Gul Bahadar group that carried out the Fateh Khel checkpost massacre. Pakistan Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir issued a concurrent statement warning that the fight against TTP and those who 'facilitate' TTP operations would continue 'until its logical conclusion' — a signal that Pakistan has not accepted the current non-escalation framework as a permanent settlement. The Taliban has not commented on the demarche, the Bannu attack, or TTP responsibility. China remains publicly silent since the May 5 Dangam civilian strike. No Urumqi Round 2 date has been set, and no formal ceasefire exists — only the fragile inter-state tactical pause that TTP mass-casualty attacks continue to erode.
footerNote: Data sourced from UNAMA, SIGAR, ACLED, Brown University Costs of War Project, US DoD, Reuters, BBC, Al Jazeera, Tolo News, Dawn, Geo News, HRW, OHCHR, OCHA
